name: Zygodactyly Type 4

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Zygodactyly Type 4

criteria.description: Presence of zygodactyly characterized by fusion of the second and third digits
Complete syndactyly involving soft tissue and bony fusion between affected digits
Radiographic evidence of bony fusion and abnormal phalangeal morphology
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical zygodactyly with complete syndactyly confirmed by radiographic findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete bony and soft tissue syndactyly of digits 2 and 3
searchTerms: complete bone and skin fusion of fingers 2 and 3
full syndactyly of index and middle fingers

pathognomonic.symptomName: Medial deviation and fusion of affected digits (zygodactyly)
searchTerms: fingers 2 and 3 fused and angled inward

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in fused digits

searchTerms: underdeveloped finger bones next to each other
bent fingers next to extra digit
abnormal nail growth on fingers or toes

occasional.symptomName: Mild soft tissue swelling around fused digits
searchTerms: soft tissue puffiness near fused digits

occasional.symptomName: Mild functional limitation in fine motor tasks

rare.symptomName: Associated syndromic features such as craniofacial anomalies
searchTerms: additional features like facial or skull abnormalities

rare.symptomName: Mild joint contractures in adjacent fingers

imaging: Radiographs showing bony fusion of phalanges 2 and 3
MRI or CT may demonstrate extent of soft tissue syndactyly
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with limb development (e.g., HOXD13) reported in some cases
other: Physical examination revealing characteristic digit fusion and deviation

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement typically limited to soft tissue
Presence of extra digits rather than fusion

redFlags: Severe functional impairment of hand requiring early intervention
Presence of associated syndromic anomalies suggesting broader genetic syndrome
Progressive joint contractures or deformities beyond fused digits
references: Fitzgerald, J. et al. (2018). Clinical and Genetic Features of Zygodactyly. Journal of Hand Surgery.
